subject: Gravity after a horizontal launch
visual_message: A horizontally launched ball curves downward because gravity changes its vertical motion. A second ball dropped simultaneously from the same height has the same vertical motion and reaches the ground at the same time, ignoring air resistance.
scene_requirement: Explain this concept with a clear animated cannon-and-ball demonstration suitable for a casual viewer or junior student. Show the horizontal launch and downward acceleration, then compare a launched ball with a dropped ball. Let the narration determine the sequence. Choose the components, their arrangement, and their motion yourself.
facts: Near Earth's surface, uniform gravitational acceleration is approximately 9.81 metres per second squared downward.
With air resistance ignored, horizontal velocity remains constant after release.
A horizontal launch has zero initial vertical velocity.
With the same starting height and zero initial vertical velocity, simultaneous released balls have equal vertical displacement at every instant.
A launched ball and a dropped ball can land in different places at the same time.
constraints: Keep the starting height, gravity and simultaneous release consistent in the comparison.
Represent freely falling balls using the deterministic projectile primitive; do not replace acceleration with constant-speed linear motion.
Use short, readable visual labels. Narration captions are added from the frozen transcript by code.
Preserve the assumptions of uniform gravity and ignored air resistance.
Request a missing component explicitly. Do not silently replace it with an unrelated asset.
